title: Flatten translation schema: locale on revision, text directly on revision-scoped tables
description: Today the schema has a sibling `*Translation` table for every revision-scoped entity (RecipeRevision, RecipeRevisionIngredient, RecipeRevisionIngredientGroup, RecipeRevisionInstructionSection, RecipeRevisionInstructionStep) plus IngredientTranslation. Decision: a single revision represents ONE locale; the locale lives on the revision and text columns move onto the non-translation tables. Multi-language recipes become multiple revisions of the same Recipe, one per locale.
design:
Schema changes:
- recipe_revisions: add `locale` column (string, 10). Drop recipe_revision_translations table.
- recipe_revision_ingredients: merge text columns from recipe_revision_ingredient_translations onto base table. Drop the translation table.
- recipe_revision_ingredient_groups: same merge + drop.
- recipe_revision_instruction_sections: same merge + drop.
- recipe_revision_instruction_steps: same merge + drop.
- ingredients: decide whether the catalog stays translated (likely yes, since ingredients are shared across recipes/locales) — leave IngredientTranslation alone unless we also want catalog-per-locale.

Code: drop the *Translation models, remove `translations()` / `*Translation` relations from the parent models, push text accessors directly onto the parent. Update RecipeLocaleSlug — slug already lived per-locale, now it can reference a specific revision (or stay keyed by recipe + locale, picking the latest published revision of that locale).

Migration strategy: this is pre-production schema work (no published recipes yet?), so a destructive forward-only migration is acceptable unless told otherwise.
acceptance_criteria:
- New migration(s) committed and `php artisan migrate:fresh` runs clean.
- All `*Translation` models removed except IngredientTranslation (or removed too, per decision).
- Filament resources still boot and the recipe edit page loads without errors.
- CLAUDE.md "Domain model" section updated to reflect the new shape.

title: Public registration page so users can sign up to author recipes
description: Filament's `AppPanelProvider` currently enables `->login()` but there is no signup path — a new user can't create an account to start authoring recipes. Add a registration flow that lands the user authenticated inside the `/app` Filament panel.
acceptance_criteria:
- `/register` (or Filament equivalent) is publicly reachable.
- Submitting valid input creates a User row and logs the user in.
- Email uniqueness + password validation enforced.
- Post-signup redirect goes to the Filament `/app` dashboard.
- Existing login flow still works.

title: Filament: full recipe editor (ingredient groups, ingredients, instruction sections + steps)
description:
The current Recipe edit page is the resource scaffold and only covers the top-level Recipe + Revision fields. The user-facing intent is "edit a full recipe" — that means in one editing surface they can manage the revision content graph: ingredient groups, ingredients within each group, instruction sections, and steps within each section.

Open design questions to settle while building:
- Editing operates on a draft revision (clone on first edit) vs. directly on a working revision — fits the append-only-once-published rule.
- Use Filament repeaters vs. relation managers per child collection.
acceptance_criteria:
- From the Recipe edit page the user can add/edit/reorder ingredient groups, add/edit/reorder ingredients within a group (with unit + quantity + optional note), add/edit/reorder instruction sections, and add/edit/reorder steps within a section.
- Sort order is preserved on save and on reload.
- Saving a published revision creates a new revision instead of mutating (append-only invariant).
- Validation: required text fields are enforced; numeric quantities accept fractions / decimals as the schema allows.

title: Define test plan for Filament panel pages
description:
Write a documented, reproducible plan for verifying the Filament panel pages behave as expected. Deliverable is the PLAN (not the test suite itself) — though where a check is cheap to automate, the plan can prescribe the automated path.

Should cover the Filament resources that exist when this is written: Recipe (list/create/edit, full editor from vispa-qte), Ingredient (list/create/edit), Unit (list/create/edit), plus auth pages (login from Filament; registration from vispa-6fq).

The plan should distinguish: (a) what's automatable via Laravel feature tests / Filament's testing helpers, (b) what needs manual smoke-test steps, (c) what regression checks to run before each release.
acceptance_criteria:
- A test-plan document exists in the repo (e.g., docs/test-plan.md) listing each Filament page and the checks for it.
- Each check is categorized automated / manual.
- For automated checks, the corresponding Filament + Laravel testing helpers are named (so future tickets can pick them up).
- The plan covers happy path + at least one error / edge case per resource (e.g., invalid input, unauthorized access).
